tasks.short: Select people or transactions for focused continuity intelligence collection.

steps.what: Review the intelligence question, collection remit and permitted sources.
Find dependency records, relevant transactions and business contacts across permitted sources.
Compare evidence and prepare a target shortlist with reasons and information gaps.

loop.input: Permitted source bundle and scope notes.
loop.output: Draft target shortlist with source-linked facts, reasons and information gaps.
loop.check: Validate identifiers and source references; a planner checks relevance, omissions and unsupported inferences.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one correction pass per bundle; unresolved evidence returns to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Incident narratives describe dependencies and relevant contacts in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Discuss operational context and choose proposed targets and collection priorities.
Approve targets, collection methods, limits and escalation conditions.
Record the approved scope and send the collection brief to assigned staff.

tasks.design: A read-only integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles permitted records from the {DOCS}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; a bounded model loop extracts source-linked facts for a draft shortlist. People choose targets and approve collection limits in the {WORKFLOW}, which generates the collection brief in the {DOCS} and routes it through the {EMAIL}. Collection itself remains a separate, explicitly scoped activity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records sit across systems, names do not always match, and selecting a target depends on context. Bespoke retrieval and document preparation previously cost more than occasional use justified.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, validation and brief templates. Bounded text extraction helps prepare evidence, without resolving the underlying judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete dependencies, ambiguous identities and restricted sources remain difficult. GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act obligations depend on intended use, while national rules may constrain employee-related collection.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently relevant person or transaction would distract from the continuity question, and judge whether further enquiry is proportionate.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of enquiries into newly exposed supplier dependencies.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling evidence and more time testing assumptions with process owners. Approval rights remain with the risk owner; no additional investigation authority is gained.

reach.task: Identify shipments whose disruption would interrupt a critical business process.
reach.learn: Shipment identifiers, route dependencies and the difference between delay signals and confirmed disruption.

reach.task: Trace a critical process to its supporting applications and interfaces.
reach.learn: Service dependency mapping, identifier matching and evidence freshness.

evidence.claim: Permission-aware retrieval, structured records and template generation can support evidence preparation.
A bounded extraction loop can prepare source-linked facts, while target selection still requires contextual human judgement.
The digest provides no direct continuity intelligence targeting case; build estimates and time reductions are design hypotheses.

assumptions: This unusual supplemental task concerns lawful continuity enquiries into relevant business contacts and transactions.
The company has a continuity planner or a risk specialist performing this work alongside other duties.
The risk owner approves sensitive collection scopes; routine authority may be delegated.
The initial build covers a limited set of accessible internal sources.
The access estimate includes employee or works-council consultation where national rules require it; formal proceedings may take longer.
Time shares favour judgement but allow substantial evidence preparation; they are estimates, not observations.
unknowns: Whether the actual remit is continuity, security, fraud or another intelligence function.
Which sources, collection methods and personal data categories are permitted.
Which role has authority to approve targets and collection limits.
Whether stable identifiers connect contacts, dependencies and transactions.
Which national rules and consultation arrangements apply.
Whether the existing {WORKFLOW} supports approvals and permission-controlled routing.
research_questions: Which recent enquiries changed a continuity decision, and what evidence made them useful?
How often does source retrieval miss relevant records or confuse identities?
Can existing {DOCS} search and templates handle enough preparation to avoid a model loop?
What review effort and omission rate does a representative pilot show?
new_work: Review extracted evidence and investigate missing or conflicting references.
Maintain source permissions, identifier mappings and connector checks.
Update brief templates and extraction instructions when collection remits change.
Apply retention limits to source bundles and decision records.
Check that routing remains within the approved collection scope.

role.altitude: The continuity planner becomes a better-prepared coordinator of focused enquiries. Business owners retain operational judgement, and risk owners retain collection approval.
reach: Logistics dependency analysis with logistics analysts.
Application dependency mapping with computer systems analysts.
skills_to_grow: Proportionate collection design and personal data handling.
Workflow configuration and extraction quality evaluation.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a weekly dependency enquiry service that helps process owners resolve emerging continuity uncertainties before disruption.
